notes.title: Weekly Update #3 2018.02.06
notes.notes:
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/c14064114e2c0657516dd3ea809d9faee220ede5.jpg

Coming at you a couple days late, I've had a busy weekend working to increase performance. This latest patch v.0.1.02m brings back our fancy vegetation system with vast improvements on performance. I've also started setting up customization settings so players can tweak and tune their settings to better fit their systems, after which the current "quality" settings will turn into recommendations. Until an interface with knobs and sliders are setup there are three new commands /quality 0, /quality 1, and /quality 2 that will change the quality settings in-game to any of the presets, 0 being Fast, 1 being Good, and 2 being Fantastic. I hope the performance is as increased for everyone's systems as it is for mine. I like to run in fantastic even at a lower framerate, but can run steadily over 100 on fast on my not-so-hot system.

Only four days left at my day job, the last being Monday of next week. Starting Tuesday I will be here full-time pushing the envelope!

Tomorrow I will be trying to setup a development build for players to opt into and push larger changes to that before pushing them live. The first big patch planned for tomorrow will remove the invisible wall at 15km out, letting players travel infinitely into the wilds! Stuff gets pretty big out there though, don't say I didn't warn you!

Thank you again to everyone that has bought a copy of Solace Crafting in this early stage, and especially to all the dedicated bug reporters helping me find things I never would have on my own!

Here are the latest patch notes:
v 0.1.02m - 2018.02.06
- Added invincibility during teleportation and world loading to prevent the possibility of starving, freezing, and generally dying before the world loads
- Returned the more robust vegetation system with performance improvements. Though still a work in progress, the framerate is better than the "standard" approach in v0.1.02l. Please let me know how it works for everyone.
- Reduced the overall amount of types of trees for increased performance, resulting in somewhat less trees overall
- Carrots and cabbages are now resources meaning they can spawn in tiers and rarities and are harvested not just picked up
- Harvesting now checks for resource collision using a line straight out of the camera measuring distance from the player instead of a sphere check in front of the player
- Fixed harvesting speed passives not working
- Changed the way enchanting tables are saved. Not sure if that's what's causing "stuck" tables yet.
- Added /quality 0, /quality 1, and /quality 2 commands to change video quality in-game until I can setup some buttons
- Fixed clouds not rendering in quality 0 (Fast)
- Fixed jump looping

You may need to restart Steam for the download to begin.

notes.title: Hotfix v 0.1.02i
notes.notes:
Due to some players experiencing very poor performance and even crashing I have removed the vegetation control system that was managing trees, grass, resources, and other flora. It really wasn't designed for a procedural open world like we have and was sending way too many instructions to video cards. In it's place I have reverted to a much more common system that doesn't look as good (especially grass) but runs fine even in big procedural environments.

This also fixes the lack of difference between the quality modes available on launch. Regardless of quality the vegetation system was bogging everything down. Now Fast runs much faster than Good, and Good much faster than Fantastic. That's around 170fps, 80fps, and 35fps for me on my Radeon GTX 450 which is by no means a high class graphics card nowadays.

As usual I don't want to force a new save game on anyone, but as the vegetation has been completely reworked any areas you may have "cleared" of resources may have resource back in them as the resources of the entire world will be regenerated as if a new game has been started. So you may have a tree in your house, and it might be awesome, or you can cut it down.

The grass is ugly, I hate it, it's one of my pet peeves, it will be improved. Tree stumps, flowers, and some other things are temporarily missing as well, but everything will make it back in much more performant. Resource LODs (draw distances) are quite low at the moment as well, I will be readjusting them.

I have also uploaded a 64 bit version of the game. My apologies that I'm not 100% sure how Steam handles that, but I think you will need to uninstall and reinstall for the x64 version to reach you. Steam should be able to recognize that your system is x32 or x64 and both versions are marked to be 'only' applicable for their appropriate systems, even though technically x64 can run x32. If you have a 1GB update, then Steam has automatically updated to the x64 bit version for you! I was unable to double-check as the developer it provides me a separate package.

I value gameplay and stability over graphics and flare. I'm sorry for the ups and downs over the past few days!

v 0.1.02i - 2018.02.03
- Fixed vSync option
- Temporarily replaced vegetation/resource control systems with a much more performant style
- Added 64 bit version

You may need to restart Steam for the download to begin and/or reinstall to upgrade to 64 bit. If you don't know whether you are on a 64 bit system you can right click on "My Computer" (Windows 7) or "This PC" (Windows 10) in the Explorer and click "Properties"

Happy Gaming!

notes.title: Hotfix v 0.1.02g
notes.notes:
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/8be5e22d3e665e5ddc412ed2e2a30ff2bef4f2fb.jpg

Beautification techniques are not really what I'm lookig to spend time on, but in upgrading some things to take care of old bugs, sometimes the improvements are more than just functional! The above shot is a sneak peak at what will be out soon!

I'm still working on finishing up the environment improvements, mostly because I want to make sure everyone has total control over them to turn things on and off. While implementing things (kicking them until they work) I came up with some decent improvements, one of which is going to take a little extra work. To go along with all of these changes I'm going to add in the better noise which gets rid of those pointy ridges that show up at seemingly random parts of the landscape. This will me a save game wipe =[

Most of these are small steps towards turning the 15km walls off again and letting people run as far as they like! Still a few more steps and things to do, but not far out now. =]

I spent most of today looking into increasing performance. Rendering the terrains is bar far the most taxing part of the game. There are major improvements down the road, a big set of which is still under development by one of the genius programmers whose tools I make use of. In the meantime, giving players the option to turn down the draw distance is back in and you can see what works best for your computer setup. Currently terrains are brought in in 512m sections, which causes a bit of a stagger, mostly when their collider is brought into the game engine, I'm looking into slicing that up further and spreading the generation of multiple terrains across more frames.

Thank you again to everyone participating in early access! I'm sorry I still have a week and a half at my day job before I can really grind through the remaining bugs and wanted features list.

notes.title: Weekly Update #2 2018.01.28
notes.notes:
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/78fef263e4df4d1f40cd4e35c615e09f66c6dca9.jpg

The majority of bugs have been squashed! Yay! The big ones anyway. There are still some crafting station and refining station bugs lingering about and a few rare occurances I'm hard at work repairing.

Some of the crash logs that I received from players were showing indications of 3rd party software in use causing problems, so I set out to update and better manage the tools that I use. The first step was adding version control to each of them which let's me see and control what gets updated to be sure all of my customization doesn't get overwritten. This has indeed done away with some of the bugs, as well as improved visuals and performance! Clouds and fog in particular are looking extra gorgeous.

I'm still finishing up the last of the integration work and am not quite ready to patch it in tonight.

On a side note I've fixed the unnatural bumpiness that seems to show up on terrains around the shore and often in the mountains. Revisiting work on the terrains however will require me to force another wipe, so I've put it off for a little later when I can get around to adding more detail to the biomes, maybe even bringing deserts back in! Then we can get some more flavored monsters in their rightful places =]

Thank you again to everyone participating in early access! Still only 11 days in, and me with my full-time job for another two weeks, but things are coming along nicely! I hope I haven't frustrated anyone too much! You have all been very kind and understanding putting up with my current schedule.

I'll be back tomorrow!
Happy gaming!

First and foremost a huge thank you to everyone participating in early access, especially in these first few days, and especially to everyone posting reports in the forums, you guys/gals are awesome.

We had a bit of a rough start with disappearing buildings, floating towers, and unwanted resource transmutations, but hopefully that is all behind us for good!

For now I want to focus on getting all of the littler problems and quirks squared away before we move onto upgrading the game itself. People are going farther and doing much more than I had imagined they would this early! There is a list of what's being worked on pinned on the forums, so check it out!

The bad news... I have to go back to my day job tomorrow. The good news, I'm going in to resign so I can focus on Solace Crafting full time. The company I'm leaving has been very good to me, and as a responsible adult I can't just walk out the door, so I may still be with them for another 2-3 weeks, but I will do my best to checkout as fast as I can. Still, I will be on here every night, plugging in as many fixes as I can with the limited time left to me after a days work.

Thank you again for your patience through this early stage!

-Malkere (Kyle)
Big Kitty Games

For now I want to focus on getting all of the littler problems and quirks squared away before we move onto upgrading the game itself. People are going farther and doing much more than I had imagined they would this early! There is a list of what's being worked on pinned on the forums, so check it out!

The bad news... I have to go back to my day job tomorrow. The good news, I'm going in to resign so I can focus on Solace Crafting full time. The company I'm leaving has been very good to me, and as a responsible adult I can't just walk out the door, so I may still be with them for another 2-3 weeks, but I will do my best to checkout as fast as I can. Still, I will be on here every night, plugging in as many fixes as I can with the limited time left to me after a days work.

Thank you again for your patience through this early stage!

-Malkere (Kyle)
Big Kitty Games

v 0.1.0g - 2018.01.18
- Added damage reports and damage particles to pigs
- Changed eating logic to let you eat/drink unless both are full
- Added VSync enable/disable in in-game settings
- Fixed saved volume settings not starting properly
- Changed the "interact" display to auto-resize based on text content
- Added option to use F "interact" to harvest resources (can be held down)

Thank you again to everyone participating in early access! This is still only the last hour of day 2! Still a few odds and ends bugs, mostly to do with inventory and bows. As well as a few mouse and joystick problems in some cases. I will get to them all as fast as I can!

One thing, buildings disappearing! This is not nice! I'm really sorry this is happening to some people and I more or less sure that it evolves around a specific encyclopedia of code that manages infinite terrain generation. Personally, infinite, procedural terrain is a -must- for me, and I've been very stubborn about that. However, at this super early stage it might be a better decision to make things static until everything is in and working well.

Please let me know what you think about this. The little bugs I can fix in five minutes to half an hour. That's a big one though and will take some time. I'm thinking at this point ensuring a solid gameplay before worrying about people travelling millions of miles is more important.

You may need to restart Steam for the download to begin.

notes.title: Darkness and light. Patch v0.0.21
notes.notes:
Darkness and light

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/d4d05bd9759ba458d8444f325bbf11b324aa5cc1.jpg

( As posted on Patreon )

When developing a game there are a lot of choices that come into play if you look at the whole picture. Animation, scripting, and dozens of other professions within what we call "game development" each can take decades to master and are constantly evolving. As a solo developer (for the time being) it's tough keeping up on any one profession, but dabbling in all of them can be very rewarding.
One thing in Solace Crafting that has not had much attention given to it yet is lighting. This past week I got in the first workings of wall and ground torches letting us setup our own sources of light. To "celebrate" this, I've made the nighttime much darker.

Ultimately I want to give much more control over lightning to players via spells, trinkets, achievements and so forth, but for now I've just added a magically permanent light to all players. Because no really, it's dark out there. I also plan to add sometime hopefully in the next two weeks the ability to color not only equipment and buildings, but torches, and player bound lights as well.

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/af8e3447dc1b80dbcfff6ee9793cd911c2ab009b.jpg

Besides lighting, one of the main components of the inventory system, what I call inventory slots, got a complete overhaul. The method I was using involved a master script trying to control all forms of inventory. These can be player equipment, player inventory, forge inventory, monster drops, treasure chests, and many other things capable of producing and storing items of all kinds. As the system grew the master script trying to be all capable was getting uglier and uglier.

Instead, now I have reworked the system to allow inventory slots to talk to one another and attend to their own needs. This way an inventory slot knows what it's capable of, for example a leg equipment slot can only accept leg armor, and only at or lower than the player's level, and if it's full it has to be able to take off what's already equipped, and so on. There is a lot of hidden logic that goes into running simple things like this that we players are used to and I'm not looking to cut corners.

Of course, for now just getting things to work properly is more important than everything working perfectly as quite a lot is still in motion and changing over time.

I plan to start making things more and more dangerous as I start implementing building damage (not building destruction), more monsters, and improving the solace upgrade/town defense quests.

Hopefully by mid-February I'll start developing full-time! Taking what is now a great start to an open world fantasy survival RPG, and turning into a full fledged content rich experience full of monsters, towns, bosses, and achievements!

I declare 2018 the year of Solace Crafting! (for me anyway =)
The year my dreams come true!
Thank you for your patronage and I wish excitement and happiness your way as well!

Full patch notes:
v 0.0.21 - 2018.01.07
- Made nighttime much darker
- Added a light to players until we are able to equip a light source
- Fixed more inventory bugs, particularly refining stations refining stuff in player inventory
- Refining high tier resources now requires higher tier fuels
- Right-clicking an item while a facilitiy windows is open will now attemp to move the item
  (won't auto-stack yet / still not working in some cases)
- Right-clicking a piece of equipment will now try to equip it
- Right-clicking a consumable in your inventory will now attempt to eat it
- Improved 'right-click to place one' to work everywhere
- Hotbar skills can now be removed by clicking and dragging them off
- Combined all UI refresh calls into single passes
- Added lots of item icons
Building----------------------
- Stopped furniture placement dummy duplicates
- Fixed furniture placement mode not turning off in some cases
Adventuring----------------------
- Added icons for Disciple skills
Harvesting----------------------
- Fixed harvesting skill point display/saving/loading
- Added a harvesting ability for each profession
- Fixed passive harvesting skills
- Added icons for all harvesting skills
- Increased amount required to level harvesting professions (still need to make it visible)
- Added resource node rarities (uncommon, rare, elite, legendary)
  Rare cannot show up until tier 2, elite until tier 4, legendary until tier 6
  Each rarity is tougher than its lessers
- Changed uncommon+ loot drop logic on resources
- Added uncommon+ resource drop chances to all rarities
Crafting----------------------
- Rare items are now crafted using uncommon+ resources instead of blessings
- Locked refining facility craftable tiers to harvesting profession levels.

notes.title: Patch 0.0.18 is live!
notes.notes:
Refining stations, crafting stations, new early game progression, and lots of little fixes as we push towards improved AI, and NPC summoning... I'm starting to eye that early access "release" button!

Check out a better description over at Patreon!

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/e9f6dfe669cf47db5e128b33f414ad88b6c9f34a.jpg

v 0.0.18 - 2017.11.21
- This update will not accept older save files. Sorry!
- Replaced built-in "splash screen" with custom company logo screen in lieu of bug reports
- Fixed a building rotation bug, still seeing another though
- Fixed an error when clicking on the drop button
- Added several icons
- Improved monster hit registry on slopes
- Added a min/max body temperature indicator in the stats display
Harvesting:
- Changed resource rare rewards to be calculated per amount harvested not per swing
- Changed cloth to stalk(raw) and thread(refined)
- Changed leather to hide(raw) and leather(refined) (will get an animal in next update)
- Changed wood to timber(raw) and lumber(refined)
- Added resource processing facilities:
  Retting Vat: stalk -> thread. Uses globe of water as fuel
  Tanning Rack: hide -> leather. Uses tannin as fuel
  Sawing Station: timber -> lumber. No fuel required
  Forge: ore -> metal. Uses timber as fuel
- Changed resource processing user interface. One fuel is used per stack refined.
- Upgrades (tier upgrade for starters) are not in yet
Crafting:
- Fixed ingredient details not showing up in recipe details interface
- Fixed recipe list scroll sensitivity
- Changed recipe list ingredient displays to dynamic strings
- Fixed being able to craft higher level items than profession level when changing selected recipe
- Added "simple" cloth, tool, and club recipes that do not require processed resources
- Some items such as torch, and campfire are also classified as simple, meaning they have no level, tier, nor rarity
- Improved item details and recipe settings to not show/allow control of levels, tiers, nor rarity for simple items
- Improved item details to not show levels on tier only items such as resources, refining stations, and crafting stations
- Improved item details to color titles based on rarity
- Added Tailoring, Leatherworking, Smithing, Woodworking, and Stonecutting crafting stations (better models pending). The crafting interface will show if a crafting station is necessary, what tier is necessary, and if those requirements are being met or not. (will give crafting stations an interface with specific recipe lists/profession details in the future, leaving the profession/recipe browser separate from the actual crafting interface)
- Added craftable infinite fuel sources: water font, tannin font, and fire font for retting, tanning, and smelting. (these will require unlocking in the future)
- Facility tiers are not yet locked because they are not yet unlockable
Temperature, Thirst, Hunger:
- Changed the radial displays to lines with numbers

notes.title: Patch v0.0.17 is live!
notes.notes:
Here are the patch notes for the latest build!
Check out more about this update on Patreon

v 0.0.17 - 2017.11.15
- This update will not accept older save files. Sorry!
- Improved /stuck command
- Fixed an error that would cause vegetation to not turn on after short teleports/recall
- Fixed an error that would cause terraforming to go way too high or way too low
- Solace level upgrades now add 100 to storage as well
- Completing a solace level or population upgrade now awards exp
- Monsters at night now move twice as fast and hit twice as hard

Temperature
- Added early air temperature system based on time of day, elevation, and area level
- Player temperature is affected by air temperature, player wetness, and wind
- Armor insulation is determined by slot, level, tier, and rarity, not type
- Insulation increases min and max temperature tolerance, not one or the other
- When cold, fullness will decrease, when hot, hydration will decrease
- Extreme hot and cold will cause physical damage

Hunger and thirst
- Added early hunger and thirst system affected time not actions
- Starvation and dehydration will cause physical damage
- Oranges, and globes of water will randomly drop off trees and fibers for now

notes.title: Update v0.0.14
notes.notes:
v 0.0.14 - 2017.10.26
- Fixed players "sticking" to walls/objects
- Change distance display to show tens of meters
- Chance for a hole in the terrain at world zero (working on new terrain system)
- Short range teleportation is working fine
- Long range teleportation (over 8km) is still bugged (working on a new terrain system)

Building:
- Changed new building placement to default 10cm from the ground instead of fully raised
- Building Foundations now must touch the ground
- Fixed building aimbox movement during typing in chat
- Fixed some instances of buildings not reloading properly
- Fixed an error preventing the reselection of buildings for continued construction
- Improved building support detection
- Reworked a lot of building colliders
- Stopped building keyboard control during chat input
- Added building slot selection keys, 1:floor, 2:center, 3:forward edge, 4: right edge, 5:back edge, 6:left edge
- Added building recipe selection move capabilities with the up and down arrow keys
- Added resource tier selection to building interface and building recipes
- Added display of available resources to buildingUI
- Added options to limit resources used to inventory or solace storage or both
- Changed Wood Roof to 3 different recipes: Wood Ramp and Wood Triangle 1 and 2
- Added Wood Obelisk (static defence) (crappy model for now, no upgrades)

Solaces:
- Changed solaces from crafted/placable facilities, to buildings
- Added upgrade interface to solaces, only level and power are upgradeable (for now)
- Added "Set As Home" button to solace upgrade menu for Recall spell
- The starter solace, or "Khora Core Shard," can no longer be renamed nor upgraded
- New solaces cannot be placed within 500m of the Khora Core Shard
- New solaces cannot be placed within 250m of one another
- Building can now spend resources from player inventory or solace network
- Spending resources from the network requires you to be within power range of a solace
- Building can now requires the tier of resources to be spent to be specified in the UI
